questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of Snowflake ML Functions such as Forecasting and Anomaly Detection?

options.text: To provide out-of-the-box machine learning analysis on structured data without requiring programming
To fine-tune large language models on unstructured text
To perform fuzzy search over documents
To manage the deployment of custom Python models

explanation.correct: ML Functions are out-of-the-box analysis tools that simplify creating and using traditional ML models on structured data, letting analysts predict and classify without programming.

distractors.B: Fine-tuning LLMs is done by Cortex Fine-tuning, not ML Functions.
distractors.C: Fuzzy search is provided by Cortex Search, not ML Functions.
distractors.D: Deploying custom Python models is the role of the Model Registry, not ML Functions.

questions.stem: Which ML Function flags metric values that differ from typical expectations in time-series data?

explanation.correct: Anomaly Detection flags metric values that differ from typical expectations, operating on time-series data.

distractors.A: Forecasting predicts future metric values from past trends, not flag anomalies.
distractors.B: Classification sorts rows into classes and does not require time-series data.
distractors.D: Top Insights finds dimensions and values that affect a metric in surprising ways, not flag anomalies over time.

questions.stem: How are models stored in the Snowflake Model Registry?

options.text: As files in an external cloud storage bucket
As first-class schema-level objects in Snowflake
As rows in a system metadata table
As account-level objects shared across all databases

explanation.correct: The Model Registry stores machine learning models as first-class schema-level objects in Snowflake, alongside other database objects.

distractors.A: Models are stored within Snowflake, not in external cloud storage buckets.
distractors.C: Models are first-class objects, not merely rows in a metadata table.
distractors.D: Models are schema-level objects, not account-level objects.

questions.stem: Which THREE capabilities are provided by Snowflake ML for the machine learning lifecycle? (Select THREE)

options.text: Feature Store for defining, managing, and serving ML features
Automatic SQL generation from natural language
Model Registry for logging and managing models
ML Observability for monitoring model performance and drift

explanation.correct: Snowflake ML provides the Feature Store, Model Registry, and ML Observability (plus ML Jobs, experiment tracking, and ML Lineage) as part of the end-to-end ML lifecycle.

distractors.B: Natural-language-to-SQL is Cortex Analyst, part of Cortex, not Snowflake ML.
distractors.D: Hybrid search is Cortex Search, part of Cortex, not Snowflake ML.
distractors.F: PII redaction is the AI_REDACT Cortex function, not a Snowflake ML capability.

questions.stem: Which TWO privileges allow a role to USE a model in the Model Registry (as opposed to creating one)? (Select TWO)

options.text: USAGE privilege (warehouse inference without seeing internals)
READ privilege (SPCS inference and viewing metadata)

explanation.correct: To use a model, you need USAGE (allows warehouse inference without seeing internals) or READ (allows SPCS inference and viewing metadata like comments, tags, metrics).

distractors.A: CREATE MODEL is required to create a model, not to use an existing one.
distractors.C: MODIFY is not one of the model usage privileges described for the registry.
distractors.E: OPERATE is not a model registry usage privilege.

questions.scenario: A data scientist calls the registry's log_model method with the same model_name but a new version_name.
questions.stem: What is the result?

options.text: An error occurs because the model name already exists
A new version of the existing model is logged
A separate model with an auto-generated name is created

explanation.correct: Calling log_model again with the same model_name but a different version_name logs an additional version of the existing model. Each model can have unlimited versions.

distractors.A: The existing model is not overwritten; a new version is added.
distractors.B: No error occurs; the combination of name and version must be unique, and a new version name is unique.
distractors.D: The model name is reused, not auto-generated, and the model is not separate.

questions.scenario: A team wants to run traditional ML training with distributed model training and hyperparameter tuning using PyTorch and XGBoost inside Snowflake.
questions.stem: Which Snowflake ML environment provides this pre-built, optimized capability?

explanation.correct: ML training runs in Container Runtime, a pre-built ML environment optimized for data loading, distributed training, and hyperparameter tuning, with preinstalled packages like PyTorch and XGBoost, accessible from Snowflake Notebooks.

distractors.B: Cortex Analyst is for text-to-SQL, not model training.
distractors.C: The Model Registry manages/serves models but is not the training environment.
distractors.D: Cortex Search Service is for search, not ML training.

questions.scenario: A model registered in the Snowflake Model Registry needs a maximum number of versions constraint verified.
questions.stem: What is the maximum number of versions a single model can have?

explanation.correct: A model in the Model Registry can have a maximum of 1000 versions.

distractors.A: 100 is not the version limit; it relates to metadata size constraints in KB.
distractors.B: 500 is the maximum number of arguments per method, not versions.
distractors.D: Versions are not unlimited; the documented limit is 1000.

questions.scenario: A data scientist is reviewing which model types are natively supported by the Model Registry's built-in types.
questions.stem: Which THREE model frameworks have built-in type support in the Model Registry? (Select THREE)

explanation.correct: The Model Registry has built-in support for common types including scikit-learn, xgboost, LightGBM, Prophet, CatBoost, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Keras, Hugging Face pipelines, Sentence Transformer, and MLFlow pyfunc models.

distractors.A: Apache Spark MLlib is not listed among the built-in supported model types.
distractors.C: Weka is not a built-in supported model type in the registry.
distractors.E: RapidMiner is not a built-in supported model type in the registry.

questions.scenario: An analyst gets an error running an ML Function and suspects a session setting is the cause.
questions.stem: Which session setting must be enabled before using ML Functions?

explanation.correct: Before using ML Functions, AUTOCOMMIT must be enabled in the session. It is enabled by default when starting a new Snowflake session.

distractors.A: QUERY_TAG is a label for queries and is unrelated to ML Function requirements.
distractors.C: USE_CACHED_RESULT controls result caching, not ML Function execution.
distractors.D: ABORT_DETACHED_QUERY is unrelated to the AUTOCOMMIT requirement for ML Functions.

questions.scenario: A data scientist logs a scikit-learn model but does not specify a version_name.
questions.stem: What happens to the version name?

options.text: The log_model call fails because version_name is required
A human-readable version name is generated automatically
The model is logged without any version

explanation.correct: If version_name is missing in log_model, a human-readable version name is generated automatically.

distractors.A: version_name is optional; log_model does not fail when it is omitted.
distractors.B: The version does not default to a fixed 'v1'; a readable name is auto-generated.
distractors.D: Logging a model always creates a version; models cannot exist without at least one version.

questions.stem: Which THREE system aliases are available in all models? (Select THREE)

explanation.correct: Every model has three system aliases: DEFAULT (default version), FIRST (oldest by creation time), and LAST (newest by creation time).

distractors.B: LATEST_STABLE is not a built-in system alias.
distractors.D: PRODUCTION is not a built-in system alias (you could create it as a custom alias).
distractors.F: CURRENT is not a built-in system alias for model versions.

questions.scenario: A data scientist wants to run inference by calling a logged model's predict method on a DataFrame in Python.
questions.stem: Which ModelVersion method is used to execute the model's method in a warehouse?

explanation.correct: mv.run() executes a model version's method (e.g., predict) in a Snowflake warehouse, passing a Snowpark or pandas DataFrame with inference data.

distractors.A: mv.load() loads the original Python model object into local memory, not runs inference in the warehouse.
distractors.C: mv.export() exports the model's files to a local directory.
distractors.D: mv.deploy() is not the method used; inference is invoked via run().

questions.scenario: A team is reviewing which SQL DDL commands are available for managing machine learning models.
questions.stem: Which THREE are valid ML model DDL commands? (Select THREE)

explanation.correct: Valid ML model DDL commands include CREATE MODEL, ALTER MODEL, SHOW MODELS, and DROP MODEL.

distractors.B: TRAIN MODEL is not a Snowflake ML model DDL command.
distractors.D: DEPLOY MODEL is not a valid DDL command; deployment/inference is handled differently.
distractors.F: PUBLISH MODEL is not a valid Snowflake DDL command.

questions.scenario: A data scientist wants to compute Shapley values to understand which input features contribute most to a model's predictions.
questions.stem: Which Snowflake ML capability provides this?

explanation.correct: ML Explainability computes Shapley values for models in the Model Registry, telling you which input features contribute most to predictions, regardless of where the model was trained.

distractors.A: ML Lineage traces artifacts from source data to features, datasets, and models, not feature contribution.
distractors.B: Feature Store manages ML features, not model explanations.
distractors.D: Experiment Tracking records training results and metrics, not Shapley-based explanations.

questions.scenario: A model was trained using a Snowflake ML Function (for example, FORECAST).
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about models trained with Snowflake ML Functions (for example, FORECAST) are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: They appear in the Model Registry and are managed by the registry API
They are automatically shared to all accounts in the organization
They do NOT appear in the Model Registry
They can be deleted individually from the Feature Store
Their backing objects have a populated instance_id in ACCOUNT_USAGE views

explanation.correct: Models trained with ML Functions do NOT appear in the Model Registry (which manages Python models). Their backing objects appear in ACCOUNT_USAGE.TABLES/STAGES with a populated instance_id and null database/schema.

distractors.A: ML Function models are not managed by the Model Registry API.
distractors.B: They are not automatically shared across the organization.
distractors.D: The backing objects are fully managed by the model instance and cannot be accessed or deleted separately, and they are not in the Feature Store.

questions.scenario: A data engineer needs to access the raw artifacts (files) backing a logged model in the registry.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about accessing model artifacts are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: USAGE privilege on a model is sufficient to access its artifacts
Ownership of the model is required to access its artifacts
Artifacts are addressed using a snow:// URL rather than standard stage path syntax
Artifacts can be modified in place after the model is logged
Artifacts are stored in an external S3 bucket owned by the user

explanation.correct: Accessing model artifacts requires ownership (USAGE is not sufficient), and artifacts are addressed using a snow:// URL (e.g., snow://model/<name>/versions/<version>/) rather than usual stage path syntax.

distractors.A: USAGE does not grant artifact access; ownership is required.
distractors.D: Artifacts cannot be modified after logging; they are immutable (though you can view or download them).
distractors.E: Artifacts are stored on an internal Snowflake stage, not an external user-owned bucket.

questions.scenario: A data scientist wants to track prediction accuracy on a model version by attaching a key-value pair like test_accuracy=0.96.
questions.stem: What is this key-value pair called in the Model Registry?

explanation.correct: Metrics are key-value pairs used to track prediction accuracy and other model version characteristics. Unlike tags, metric names and values do not need to be predefined.

distractors.A: Tags must be predefined with CREATE TAG and record purpose/lifecycle info, not accuracy values freely.
distractors.C: A comment is descriptive text, not a structured key-value metric.
distractors.D: A signature defines the model method's input/output structure, not accuracy tracking.

questions.scenario: An ML team wants to deploy a logged model for inference and is choosing target platforms.
questions.stem: Which TWO are valid target platforms for a model in the registry? (Select TWO)

explanation.correct: The acceptable target platforms are combinations of WAREHOUSE and SNOWPARK_CONTAINER_SERVICES. Models can run in a warehouse for inference or be served in Snowpark Container Services for GPU-based inference.

distractors.A: EXTERNAL_LAMBDA is not a valid target platform for registry models.
distractors.D: EDGE_DEVICE is not a supported target platform.
distractors.E: SERVERLESS_TASK is not a valid model target platform.

questions.scenario: A team wants to monitor a deployed model's performance and detect drift over time using SQL DDL.
questions.stem: Which command creates the object used for this monitoring?

explanation.correct: CREATE MODEL MONITOR creates a model monitor, which allows monitoring the performance of ML models deployed in Snowflake (part of the ML model DDL).

distractors.A: CREATE MODEL VERSION is not the monitoring command; versions are added via ALTER MODEL ... ADD VERSION.
distractors.C: CREATE DRIFT DETECTOR is not a valid Snowflake command.
distractors.D: CREATE MODEL ALERT is not a valid Snowflake DDL command.
